correctness.rationale: For a super dominating set S, its omitted roots U cannot have omitted private leaves because an omitted leaf would lack a selected neighbor. Any selected root may support at most one omitted private leaf, and if it does, no adjacent base root may be omitted or the root would have two omitted neighbors. Conversely selecting all other vertices witnesses each omitted root by any own selected leaf (r_v>=1), and each allowable omitted leaf by its selected root. This gives a bijection with U and zero/one leaf choices at v outside N[U]. Counting selected vertices gives R+|N(U)\U| plus factors x+r_v. Constant term requires U a component union, yielding the component product. With two omissions, disallowed pairs are two leaves of one bundle, root/own leaf, and neighbor root/leaf, yielding the coefficient formula. Independent direct defining-predicate brute force agreed with the polynomial on all 74 base/multiplicity instances n<=3, including isolated/disconnected roots. No claim that finite checks prove arbitrary n.
